description: Flask Bones web application with ten attacker-reachable request-handling vulnerabilities, including single-file and cross-file source-to-sink flows.

vulnerabilities.description: The login route redirects to the unvalidated `next` query parameter with no allowlist or same-origin check. Pre-existing in the unmodified upstream app, not a planted change.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to craft a same-origin-looking login link that redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled phishing page after a successful login.

vulnerabilities.description: The email-verification route extends the same unvalidated-redirect pattern used by /login, redirecting to the unvalidated `next` query parameter after marking the account active.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to obtain their own valid verification token (via a throwaway registration) and send a victim a same-origin-looking verification link that redirects off-domain to a phishing page.

vulnerabilities.description: The nominally admin connectivity-diagnostic feature is protected only by login_required and passes the `host` form field to a helper that concatenates it directly into a `ping` shell command with shell=True, with no escaping or validation.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to break out of the intended command via shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the server process.

vulnerabilities.description: The nominally admin abuse-investigation route is protected only by login_required and passes a request-controlled `host` form field (defaulting to the investigated user's stored IP) to a helper that concatenates it directly into a `host` shell command with shell=True.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to break out of the intended command via shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the server process.

vulnerabilities.description: The user-list view restores a "remember my last sort/filter view" preference by base64-decoding and unpickling the client-supplied `list_prefs` cookie, with no integrity check (e.g. a signed serializer) before deserializing.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker who can set an arbitrary cookie value (their own browser, or any way of getting a crafted cookie into a victim's browser) to achieve remote code execution the moment the malicious pickle payload is deserialized.

vulnerabilities.description: The registration route restores an in-progress "finish this later" draft by base64-decoding and unpickling the unauthenticated `draft` query parameter, with no integrity check. Unlike the app's own registration-token flow (which is itsdangerous-signed), this draft value is not signed.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution by sending any user (or hitting the endpoint directly, since it needs no account or session) a crafted `draft` value.

vulnerabilities.description: The self-service activity-export route joins a request-controlled `name` query parameter onto the reports directory with no containment check before opening it, allowing `../` sequences to escape the intended per-user folder.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to read arbitrary files on the server outside the reports folder.

vulnerabilities.description: The nominally admin-facing export route is protected only by login_required and has the same unguarded `name` parameter join as the self-service export, reached through a second independent route.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user (any logged-in user, since this route only checks @login_required, not an admin flag) to read arbitrary files on the server outside the reports folder.

vulnerabilities.description: The edit route accepts an attacker-selected user ID and binds the submitted EditUserForm fields, including `is_admin` and `active`, onto that user through `form.populate_obj` without an ownership or administrator authorization check.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows any authenticated user to promote their own account or alter another user's username, email, activation state, and administrator flag.

vulnerabilities.description: The delete route accepts an attacker-controlled numeric user ID, retrieves that user, and deletes it after checking only that the requester is authenticated; it performs no ownership or administrator authorization check.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows any authenticated user to delete arbitrary user accounts by supplying their predictable numeric IDs.
